title: Playtesters believed my characters were purely hand modeled... they were wrong
author: TheGamingSpringbok
selftext:
In my upcoming game Twilight Tavern (which just reached 400 wishlists yayy), I use AI tools to assist in the creation of certain 3D characters.

I made a little bet with my playtesters.

I asked them to carefully look at one of the characters and determine whether it was AI-generated or not. After thinking about it, they answered "Nope, because x, y, z."

Technically, they neither won nor lost the bet. The character was handmade with the assistance of AI tools. When I explained this, they were quite surprised.

One playtester even said, "So it's an AI character? But it doesn't feel like it."

This made me realise two things:

1. Bro was so quick to label something as an "AI character" despite my explanation of how it was created 😂😭
2. The fact that it didn't feel like AI was reassuring, considering the effort I've put into maintaining a consistent art style and direction.

This experience also reinforced my opinion on playtesting.

I personally find observing players' actual experiences and emotions more valuable than simply handing them a questionnaire.

After all, yknow the saying "judge someone by their actions, not their words"? I think this applies to playtesting to some extent as well.

Watching players experience joy, frustration, curiosity or excitement can sometimes tell me more about my game than their written feedback alone.

I'm still slightly concerned that Twilight Tavern will face more scrutiny online simply because it has an AI disclosure. However, seeing games like Slotbound and Ebbtide gain traction despite their disclosures is somewhat reassuring.

Anyway, I thought I'd share this little experience with fellow devs who are also experimenting with AI tools in their development process.
